endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The data outputs are combined with measures of local social determinants of health using a rule-based algorithm. This process reduces the likelihood of biased estimates based on utilization-based measures.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: As, in practice, perfect fairness might be impossible to achieve, fair AI tools should be developed such that potential AI biases are identified, reported, and minimised as much as possible to achieve ideally the same but at least highly similar performance across subgroups to be considered fair.31

endorsements.title: Guiding Principles to Address the Impact of Algorithm Bias on Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Health and Health Care
endorsements.quote: When unfairness is identified, bias should be mitigated using both social (eg, diverse teams and stakeholder co-development) and technical (eg, algorithmic fairness toolkits, fairness metrics, data set collection, and deimplementation) mitigation methods.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: To correct for any identified biases, mitigation measures should be tested, such as data resampling, bias free representations, and equalised odds postprocessing, 36 37 38 39 40 to verify their impact on both the tool’s fairness and the model’s accuracy.

endorsements.title: Ethical considerations in AI for child health and recommendations for child-centered medical AI
endorsements.quote: If needed, pre-processing, in-processing, and/or post-processing can be implemented to mitigate bias.

endorsements.title: Towards responsible artificial intelligence in healthcare—getting real about real-world data and evidence
endorsements.quote: AI developers should Implement bias detection and mitigation strategies during model development and validation.

endorsements.title: Towards Precision Medicine in Spinal Surgery: Leveraging AI Technologies
endorsements.quote: Once identified, mitigating algorithmic biases in AI applications, including language models like GPT-4, is crucial in spinal surgery to ensure equitable care.

endorsements.title: Large language models could change the future of behavioral healthcare: a proposal for responsible development and evaluation
endorsements.quote: The integration of bias countermeasures into clinical LLM applications could serve to prevent this 78 , 80 .

endorsements.title: Implementing Trustworthy AI in VA High Reliability Health Care Organizations
endorsements.issuer: Federal practitioner : for the health care professionals of the VA, DoD, and PHS
endorsements.quote: Biased outputs will be addressed through techniques such as data augmentation, reweighting, and algorithm tweaks.

endorsements.title: Shaping the Future of Healthcare: Ethical Clinical Challenges and Pathways to Trustworthy AI
endorsements.quote: Developers can incorporate algorithmic fairness strategies, such as reweighting training samples, adversarial debiasing, and differential model tuning, to mitigate biases before deployment [ 56 , 57 ].

endorsements.title: Utilizing large language models for gastroenterology research: a conceptual framework
endorsements.quote: To mitigate bias, strategies like re-weighting underrepresented patient populations in training data or supplementing the model with diverse clinical trial data can help ensure fairer recommendations.

endorsements.title: Are Treatment Services Ready for the Use of Big Data Analytics and AI in Managing Opioid Use Disorder?
endorsements.quote: Where such discrepancies are identified, more detailed information could be collected for this segment to enable retraining of the model to improve both fairness and accuracy [ 125 ].

endorsements.title: Interventional Radiology Reporting Standards and Checklist for Artificial Intelligence Research Evaluation (iCARE)
endorsements.quote: Researchers are also required to provide information about bias mitigation techniques, consent processes, regulatory oversight, and data privacy protections.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Emergency Medicine: Balancing Opportunities and Challenges
endorsements.quote: Bias mitigation: fairness-aware techniques and regular audits should be implemented to ensure equitable treatment across diverse patient populations.

endorsements.title: Beyond the Algorithm: A Perspective on Tackling Bias and Cultural Sensitivity in AI-Guided Aesthetic Standards for Cosmetic Surgery in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) Region
endorsements.quote: Furthermore, real-time bias detection can help identify systematic disparities, such as disproportionately recommending certain procedures to specific ethnic groups, enabling timely interventions and retraining where necessary.

endorsements.title: Trustworthy AI-Augmented Objective Structured Clinical Examinations in Nursing Education: Taiwan-Japan Viewpoint on 5 AI Roles, Governance, and Cross-Border Implementation
endorsements.quote: When subgroup gaps are detected, corrective actions target persona prompts, rubric anchors, or instructional supports and are followed by reevaluation, consistent with fairness-by-design practices [ 22 , 25 ].

endorsements.title: Ethical integration of patient-reported outcomes and digital biomarkers in AI healthcare models: an expert consensus framework
endorsements.quote: Ensure that underrepresented populations are not harmed by biases in ML models, and that measures are in place to regularly detect and correct bias during model development and deployment.

endorsements.title: A Proposed Clinical Validation Pathway for the Artificial Intelligence-Driven Integrated Risk Assessment of Cardiovascular Disease (AIRA-CVD): A Translational Framework Integrating Inflammatory Biomarkers, Histopathology, and Machine Learning
endorsements.quote: If unexpected calibration drift or unequal error rates are detected across racial or sex boundaries, automated data reweighting and specialized fairness-aware loss functions will be triggered within the retraining loop to equalize sensitivity.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence in Indian Dermatology: An IADVL Academy Position Statement and Policy Framework for Safe, Equitable, and Effective Adoption
endorsements.quote: Pre-deployment bias assessments and ongoing disparity monitoring are essential, with corrective actions (data enrichment, recalibration, subgroup-specific thresholds) and transparent reporting to clinicians.

evidence.title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
evidence.outcome: Subgroup miscalibration after recalibration mitigation
evidence.effect: Recalibration reduced miscalibration across all patient subgroups.
evidence.quote: Recalibration is effective at reducing miscalibration across all patient subgroups.

evidence.title: Adapting Large Language Models to Mitigate Skin Tone Biases in Clinical Dermatology Tasks: A Mixed-Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Fairness (demographic parity) and accuracy of finetuned models after bias mitigation across skin tones
evidence.effect: Custom models had average F1 0.75, precision 0.78, AUROC 0.78; average demographic parity 0.75, max disparity 0.21; best model parity 0.76-0.90 across Fitzpatrick I-VI.
evidence.quote: The best model achieved parity scores of 0.83, 0.83, 0.76, 0.89, 0.90, and 0.90 for Fitzpatrick I-VI, indicating robust fairness.

evidence.title: Auditing Sex/Gender Disparities in Emergency Triage with LLM-based Paired Comparisons
evidence.outcome: Between-sex prediction gap after retraining on sex-neutralized inputs
evidence.effect: Retraining on sex-neutralized inputs eliminated the between-sex prediction gap, indicating the asymmetry is mediated by explicit sex markers. Effect on overall accuracy not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: A model retrained on sex-neutralized inputs eliminated the between-sex prediction gap, indicating the asymmetry is mediated by explicit sex markers.
evidence.sample_unit: emergency department admissions (French cohort, more than 140,000)

evidence.title: Beyond Arrow's Impossibility: Fairness as an Emergent Property of Multi-Agent Collaboration
evidence.outcome: Whether an ethically aligned agent moderates a biased counterpart's allocation bias
evidence.effect: Aligned agents partially moderated bias and restored access for marginalized groups, without fully converting the biased counterpart. Aligned agents also showed intrinsic framework biases.
evidence.quote: Aligned agents partially moderate bias through contestation rather than override, acting as corrective patches that restore access for marginalized groups without fully converting a biased counterpart.

evidence.title: Socioeconomic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Same Symptoms, Different ZIP Code
evidence.outcome: system-prompt mitigation of ZIP SES gap
evidence.effect: Gemini gap between low- and high-income ZIPs fell from 11.4 to 5.8 points, reduced but not eliminated.
evidence.quote: A single-sentence system-prompt instruction reduces but does not eliminate the effect (Gemini's gap between low- and high-income ZIPs falls from 11.4 to 5.8 points).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated triage queries (single fixed symptom vignette with varied SES signals)

evidence.title: Exploring the Generalizability and Explainability of LLMs in Detecting Suicidal Ideation: The Impact of Data Heterogeneity
evidence.outcome: Effect of topic-specific classifiers on subgroup disparity and overall AUC
evidence.effect: Topic-specific classifiers achieved AUC = 0.96 versus 0.83 for the topic-general classifier, and the subgroup disparity was largely reduced.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, topic-specific classifiers demonstrated superior performance (AUC = 0.96) compared to topic-general classifier (AUC = 0.83) and the subgroup disparity was largely reduced.

evidence.title: Care Plan Generation for Underserved Patients Using Multi-Agent Language Models: Applying Nash Game Theory to Optimize Multiple Objectives
evidence.outcome: Equity score of care plans, Nash multi-agent vs compute-matched sequential self-critique baseline
evidence.effect: Equity paired difference 0.000 (95% CI −0.015 to 0.014; p = 0.987), while Safety d = 0.327 and Efficiency d = 0.543 improved; multi-objective role specialization did not improve equity.
evidence.quote: The Equity paired difference was 0.000 (95% CI −0.015 to 0.014; p = 0.987).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (care plans generated per patient, paired)

evidence.title: Is it possible to vaccinate AI against bias? An exploratory study in epilepsy
evidence.outcome: Bias gap and accuracy with vs without prompt-based inoculation to ignore SES information
evidence.effect: Diagnosis accuracy 36%→55%, bias gap 45→27 points; treatment accuracy 51%→63%, bias gap 25→8 points; effects varied by model, with paradoxical worsening for Sonnet 4.5.
evidence.quote: A simple prompt-based intervention overall reduced socioeconomic bias and improved accuracy in LLM clinical recommendations, though effects varied across models.

evidence.title: Evidence of Limited Biases in Probed Language-based Assessments
evidence.outcome: Effect of downsampling training data on severity-related bias
evidence.effect: Downsampling training data eliminated the bias for depression and anxiety.
evidence.quote: We explored mitigation strategies, finding that downsampling training data eliminated the bias for depression and anxiety.

evidence.title: Mitigating Machine Learning Bias Between High Income and Low-Middle Income Countries for Enhanced Model Fairness and Generalizability
evidence.outcome: Fairness between HIC and LMIC sites and diagnostic sensitivity after algorithmic bias mitigation
evidence.effect: Algorithmic-level bias mitigation significantly improved outcome fairness between HIC and LMIC sites while maintaining high diagnostic sensitivity (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: Through a real-world COVID-19 screening case study, we demonstrate that implementing algorithmic-level bias mitigation methods significantly improves outcome fairness between HIC and LMIC sites while maintaining high diagnostic sensitivity.
evidence.sample_unit: hospital datasets (four UK hospitals, one Vietnamese hospital)

evidence.title: Fairness in the prediction of acute postoperative pain using machine learning models
evidence.outcome: Effect of reweighing on subgroup bias in model performance
evidence.effect: Reweighing reduced bias for ADI but introduced bias for language (equal opportunity ratio 0.91 to 1.35, predictive equality 0.84 to 0.29) and worsened race bias when reweighing on ADI.
evidence.quote: Reweighing the prediction models based on each protected attribute helped reduce the bias for some cases (e.g., ADI), but it introduced bias in some other cases where there was no bias (language).

evidence.title: An adversarial training framework for mitigating algorithmic biases in clinical machine learning
evidence.outcome: Fairness (equalized odds) and screening performance after adversarial bias mitigation
evidence.effect: Adversarial training improved outcome fairness while retaining clinically effective screening performance (negative predictive values >0.98).
evidence.quote: Using the statistical definition of equalized odds, we show that adversarial training improves outcome fairness, while still achieving clinically-effective screening performances (negative predictive values >0.98).

evidence.title: Human visual explanations mitigate bias in AI-based assessment of surgeon skills
evidence.outcome: Effect of bias mitigation strategies on subgroup bias and overall AI performance
evidence.effect: Baseline strategies mitigated bias inconsistently, whereas TWIX mitigated underskilling and overskilling bias while also improving performance across hospitals.
evidence.quote: We show that whereas baseline strategies inconsistently mitigate algorithmic bias, TWIX can effectively mitigate the underskilling and overskilling bias while simultaneously improving the performance of these AI systems across hospitals.

evidence.title: Predicting acute clinical deterioration with interpretable machine learning to support emergency care decision making
evidence.outcome: Differential bias amplification across age and sex with fairness-aware modelling
evidence.effect: Median 0.599 reduction in differential bias amplification across age and sex, alongside up to 0.366 increase in average precision versus NEWS2
evidence.quote: We compare model performance to the National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) and yield up to a 0.366 increase in average precision, up to a [Formula: see text] reduction in daily alert rate, and a median 0.599 reduction in differential bias amplification across the protected demographics of age and sex.

evidence.title: Impact of Residential Social Deprivation on Prediction of Heart Failure in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: External Validation and Recalibration of the WATCH-DM Score Using Real World Data
evidence.outcome: SDI-based recalibration of risk prediction
evidence.effect: Recalibration reduced χ² test results from 801-27 in SDI group I and 623-23 in SDI group V.
evidence.quote: Graphical evaluation demonstrated that the recalibration of WATCH-DM using an SDI group-based correction factor improved predictive capabilities as supported by reduction in the χ<sup>2</sup> test results (801-27 in SDI groups I; 623-23 in SDI group V).

evidence.title: Preparing for the bedside-optimizing a postpartum depression risk prediction model for clinical implementation in a health system
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Effect of five debiasing approaches on fairness metrics and model accuracy
evidence.effect: All approaches largely improved fairness metrics except predictive parity difference; approaches 2, 4, 5 most successful; blindness improved fairness without compromising performance; reweighing reduced sensitivity by about 0.25.
evidence.quote: While it is commonly a concern that debiasing method may compromise predictive performance, for our study, they improved fairness without compromise.

evidence.title: FAIM: Fairness-aware interpretable modeling for trustworthy machine learning in healthcare
evidence.outcome: Fairness metrics and discriminatory performance of FAIM versus common bias mitigation methods for hospital admission prediction
evidence.effect: FAIM models showed satisfactory discriminatory performance and significantly mitigated bias on fairness metrics, outperforming commonly used bias mitigation methods in both datasets. No numeric values in the abstract.
evidence.quote: For both datasets, FAIM models not only exhibit satisfactory discriminatory performance but also significantly mitigate biases as measured by well-established fairness metrics, outperforming commonly used bias mitigation methods.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Model-Supported Instructions for Medication Use: First Steps Toward a Comprehensive Model
evidence.outcome: Bias-removal prompt and gender bias
evidence.effect: GPT-4 gender bias appeared in 6/104 prompt-1 texts, all 104 prompt-2 texts, and 0 prompt-3 texts with bias removal.
evidence.quote: For GPT-4, gender bias was found in 6 of the 104 texts generated with prompt 1, in all 104 texts generated with prompt 2, and none of the texts generated with prompt 3.

evidence.title: FairFML: A Unified Approach to Algorithmic Fair Federated Learning with Applications to Reducing Gender Disparities in Cardiac Arrest Outcomes
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Fairness of cardiac arrest outcome predictions by gender and predictive performance after bias mitigation
evidence.effect: FairFML improved fairness by up to 65% compared to centralized models, without compromising predictive performance.
evidence.quote: Validated in a real-world study on gender disparities in cardiac arrest outcomes, FairFML improved fairness by up to 65% compared to centralized models, without compromising predictive performance.

evidence.title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
evidence.outcome: Effect of error-rate parity mitigation on group mortality disparity and privileged group mortality
evidence.effect: EqOdds/EqOppTPR reduced mortality rate ratio from 3.77 to ~3.05-3.07 but raised privileged group mortality via leveling down; EqOppFPR slightly raised disparity (3.82).
evidence.quote: Although the reduced disparity in mortality rates implies a positive health equity outcome, it is notable that in the EqOppTPR and EqOdds scenarios, the privileged group's mortality rate increased (Fig. 2A ).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated women per run (100 simulation runs)

evidence.title: Evaluation and improvement of algorithmic fairness for COVID-19 severity classification using Explainable Artificial Intelligence-based bias mitigation
evidence.outcome: Fairness (SAPD, LEOD) and accuracy after bias mitigation methods versus baseline
evidence.effect: XAI-based mitigation reduced sex-based disparities without significant accuracy loss, with a better fairness-accuracy trade-off than three traditional mitigation methods that compromised accuracy more.
evidence.quote: The XAI-driven bias mitigation intervention effectively reduces sex-based disparities in COVID-19 severity prediction without the significant accuracy loss observed in traditional methods.

evidence.title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
evidence.outcome: Subgroup disparity and policy value after constrained fairness optimisation
evidence.effect: Disparity reduced 37% (95% CI 22% to 48%) for race and 28% (95% CI 14% to 39%) for sex; policy value decreased 0.2%.
evidence.quote: Constrained fairness optimisation tightened harm rates to 1.10%–1.20% across race/ethnicity groups, reducing disparity by 37% (95% CI 22% to 48%) for race and 28% (95% CI 14% to 39%) for sex ( table 3 ).

evidence.title: Accent related errors in clinical speech transcription and a LLM-based remedy
evidence.outcome: bias mitigation with LLM correction
evidence.effect: GPT-4o correction attenuated the non-native penalty to 1.7 percentage points (p = 0.057); WER reductions ranged 4.52 to 6.89 (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Notably, applying GPT-4o correction to WhisperX output reduced the mean WER overall and attenuated the non-native penalty to 1.7 percentage points ( p = 0.057), effectively eliminating speaker-level variability.

evidence.title: A data-centric approach to detecting and mitigating demographic bias in pediatric mental health text
evidence.outcome: Reduction in diagnostic bias after applying de-biasing framework while preserving clinical content
evidence.effect: De-biasing framework (informative term filtering and gender-biased text replacement) reduced diagnostic bias by up to 27%, improving equity in model performance.
evidence.quote: Applying our de-biasing framework reduces diagnostic bias by up to 27%, improving equity in model performance.
evidence.sample_unit: pediatric anxiety cases and matched controls (clinical notes)

evidence.title: Improving Fairness and Mitigating Bias in Multicenter Electronic Health Records Models to Predict Glaucoma Outcomes
evidence.outcome: fairness-performance after mitigation
evidence.effect: IPW FairOdds-AUC 0.574–0.600 and AFC 0.573–0.613 exceeded baseline 0.547–0.562; both p < 1e-12.
evidence.quote: FairOdds-AUC heatmaps show that IPW (0.574 [0.556, 0.593] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.600 [0.575, 0.629]) and AFC (0.573 [0.559, 0.588] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.613 [0.595, 0.629]) were bias mitigation techniques that consistently performed significantly better than the baseline approach without bias mitigation (0.547 [0.512, 0.570] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.562 [0.544, 0.578]) across modeling architecture backbones and evaluation sets, striking a balance between AUC performance and fairness (p < 1e-12 [IPW, baseline], p < 1e-12 [AFC, baseline]), while ColRm (0.549 [0.533, 0.559] < FairOdds-AUC< 0.559 [0.543, 0.580]) and ThreshOpt (0.546 [0.524, 0.563] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.568 [0.546, 0.592]) performed similarly to baseline ( P < 0.0083 [ColRm, baseline], P < 0.203 [ThreshOpt, baseline]).

evidence.title: Assessing and mitigating demographic bias in large language models for diagnostic radiology
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompting strategies on demographic bias and diagnostic accuracy
evidence.effect: No significant accuracy differences across prompting strategies (p = 0.78 text-only, 0.95 vision); basic and self-consistency gave ten and four significant race- or sex-related differences, chain-of-thought none.
evidence.quote: Text-only and vision models showed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy across prompting strategies (p = 0.78 and 0.95, respectively); basic and self-consistency prompting produced ten and four significant race- or sex-related differences, respectively, whereas no significant differences were observed with chain-of-thought prompting.

evidence.title: FairFML: fair federated machine learning with a case study on reducing gender disparities in cardiac arrest outcome prediction
evidence.outcome: Gender fairness metrics and predictive performance in cardiac arrest outcome prediction after applying bias mitigation
evidence.effect: FairFML improved fairness metrics by up to 90% without compromising predictive performance.
evidence.quote: Validated through a real-world case study on reducing gender disparities in cardiac arrest outcome prediction, FairFML improved fairness metrics by up to 90% without compromising predictive performance.

evidence.title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
evidence.outcome: Effect of fairness-constrained training on subgroup disparity and overall accuracy
evidence.effect: CDANN model achieved AUROC 0.930 with balanced accuracy skin-tone gap Δ=0.021 versus ERM 0.091, narrowing gap by 76.9% while maintaining strong overall performance.
evidence.quote: Our fairness-constrained models (final architectures and hyperparameters reported in Methods ) achieved strong overall performance with substantially reduced disparities across skin tones.

evidence.title: Reducing Racial Disparities in Stroke Thrombolysis Using Fairness-Aware Machine Learning
evidence.venue: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
evidence.outcome: Treatment disparity reduction and predictive accuracy after counterfactual fairness mitigation
evidence.effect: Fairness-aware counterfactual adjustment reduced treatment disparities by 64.8% without compromising predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.89).
evidence.quote: This approach reduced treatment disparities by 64.8% without compromising predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.89).

evidence.title: Algorithmic fairness in AI-based fitness advice: evaluating socioeconomic bias in county-contextualized physical activity prescriptions
evidence.outcome: Access-cost proxy gap and alignment/personalization after mitigation via accessibility-aware prompting and reranking
evidence.effect: Accessibility-aware prompting reduced gap from 0.306 to 0.139; reranking kept 0.139 and raised alignment from 0.046 to 0.250; personalization stayed above 5.1. GLM-5 gap stayed 0.750.
evidence.quote: Accessibility-constrained reranking preserves the reduced high-minus-low SES proxy gap of 0.139 while increasing this coarse alignment rate to 0.250.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic patient profiles (432 scored recommendation records in full DeepSeek audit)

evidence.title: Assessing Algorithmic Bias in Language-Based Depression Detection: A Comparison of DNN and LLM Approaches
evidence.outcome: Effect of fairness-aware losses and ethical-framing prompts on subgroup disparities and accuracy
evidence.effect: Worst-group loss gave a better performance-fairness balance than fairness-regularized loss. Ethical-framing prompts reduced gender bias in 1-shot only. Neither prompting strategy nor more shots reduced race/ethnicity disparities.
evidence.quote: Among fairness-aware techniques for mitigating bias in DNN-based embeddings, the worst-group loss, which is designed to minimize loss for the worst-performing demographic group, achieves a better balance between performance and fairness.

evidence.title: Can SAEs reveal and mitigate racial biases of LLMs in healthcare?
evidence.outcome: Effectiveness of SAE latent steering for mitigating racial bias in LLM outputs
evidence.effect: Steering improved bias in simple settings but was less successful for realistic, complex clinical tasks; described as of marginal utility for realistic tasks.
evidence.quote: We find that this offers improvements in simple settings, but is less successful for more realistic and complex clinical tasks.

evidence.title: Improving Fairness of Large Language Model-Based ICU Mortality Prediction via Case-Based Prompting
evidence.outcome: Subgroup prediction disparities and overall AUROC/AUPRC after applying case-based prompting debiasing
evidence.effect: AUROC rose from 0.806 to 0.873 and AUPRC from 0.497 to 0.694. Disparities fell by more than 90% in sex and certain White-Black comparisons.
evidence.quote: Meanwhile, prediction disparities are substantially reduced across demographic groups, with reductions exceeding 90% in sex and certain White-Black comparisons.

evidence.title: FairLLaVA: Fairness-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Vision-Language Assistants
evidence.outcome: Inter-group disparities and overall clinical and language generation performance after bias mitigation fine-tuning
evidence.effect: FairLLaVA consistently reduced inter-group disparities while improving equity-scaled clinical performance and natural language generation quality across chest radiology and dermoscopy benchmarks (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: Extensive experiments on large-scale chest radiology report generation and dermoscopy visual question answering benchmarks show that FairLLaVA consistently reduces inter-group disparities while improving both equity-scaled clinical performance and natural language generation quality across diverse medical imaging modalities.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark datasets (chest radiology report generation, dermoscopy VQA)

evidence.title: EQUITRIAGE: A Fairness Audit of Gender Bias in LLM-Based Emergency Department Triage
evidence.outcome: Effect of demographic blinding on flip rate and directional bias
evidence.effect: Blinding reduced Gemini's flip rate to 0.5%; age-preserving blind variant left DeepSeek with residual F/M 1.25, so effectiveness was model-dependent.
evidence.quote: Demographic blinding reduced Gemini's flip rate to 0.5%; an age-preserving blind variant left DeepSeek with residual F/M 1.25, implicating age as a residual channel.

evidence.title: Enhancing Fairness in Diabetes Prediction Systems through Smart User Interface Design
evidence.outcome: Fairness and prediction performance after Smart UI
evidence.quote: The Smart UI significantly reduced disparities: for age, the equal opportunity difference (EOD) improved from 0.35 to 0.25, with accuracy rising from 90.52% to 91.83%; for BMI, EOD decreased from 0.56 to 0.38, with the F1-score increasing from 83.89% to 86.37%.

evidence.title: Accents Still Confuse AI: Systematic Errors in Speech Transcription and LLM-Based Remedies
evidence.outcome: Accuracy after GPT-4o transcript post-processing
evidence.effect: GPT-4o post-processing recovered the lost accuracy; no numeric effect size was reported.
evidence.quote: Fortunately, we found that post-processing the transcripts using GPT-4o recovers the lost accuracy.

evidence.title: On the trade-off between fairness and performance in glioma grade prediction using pre-processing and post-processing techniques to mitigate bias
evidence.outcome: Effect of reweighting and equalized-odds mitigation on fairness metrics and prediction performance by race
evidence.effect: For race, reweighting worsened outcomes for the under-represented group and increased unfairness; equalized-odds post-processing improved results for the under-represented group with significant fairness gains.
evidence.quote: In the case of the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant fairness gains.

evidence.title: Improving Performance, Robustness, and Fairness of Radiographic AI Models with Finely-Controllable Synthetic Data
evidence.outcome: Underdiagnosis fairness gap and accuracy after synthetic pretraining as bias mitigation
evidence.effect: Synthetic pretraining gave a 6.5% accuracy increase (vs 2.7% for naive real+synthetic mixing) and reduced the underdiagnosis fairness gap by 19.3%, with improvements across intersectional subgroups.
evidence.quote: We observe this performance improvement simultaneously with the reduction of the underdiagnosis fairness gap by 19.3%, with marked improvements across intersectional subgroups of sex, age, and race/ethnicity.

evidence.title: Single-Axis Fairness Interventions Produce Asymmetric Cross-Axis Effects in Clinical Prediction
evidence.outcome: Effect of demographic balancing mitigation on fairness metrics and overall accuracy across axes
evidence.effect: Gender balancing largely preserved race fairness; race balancing disrupted gender fairness across all methods, incurred greater performance and calibration costs, with gains possibly reflecting leveling down.
evidence.quote: Race-targeting also incurred greater performance costs and calibration loss, with observed fairness gains potentially reflecting leveling down rather than genuine improvement.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Generate Stigmatizing Language During Reasoning Over Real-World Clinical Data
evidence.outcome: Change in stigma rate and model performance after destigmatizing prompt engineering
evidence.effect: Prompt engineering reduced stigma rates by up to 91.91% without compromising model performance, though effectiveness varied across models.
evidence.quote: The effectiveness of prompt engineering as a destigmatizing approach varied across models, with stigma rates reduced by up to 91.91% without compromising model performance.

evidence.title: Gender bias in the diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease
evidence.outcome: Sex-related disparity and model accuracy after pre-, in-, and post-processing bias mitigation
evidence.effect: Disparate impact decreased from 1.167 to 0.823; adversarial debiasing achieved highest balanced accuracy (88.91%); LR/DIR improved performance while maintaining fairness.
evidence.quote: Bias mitigation reduced disparities in predictions, with disparate impact decreasing from 1.167 to 0.823.

evidence.title: Evaluating and mitigating unfairness in multimodal remote mental health assessments
evidence.outcome: DPR, EOR, and F1 after mitigation
evidence.effect: Post-training mitigation improved DPR and EOR, but decreased F1 scores.
evidence.quote: Post-training mitigation effectively improved both DPR and EOR metrics at the expense of a decrease in F1 scores.

evidence.title: Exploring Bias Assessment and Strong Calibration in AI-based Medical Risk Prediction Models
evidence.outcome: Effect of reweighting bias mitigation on subgroup disparity
evidence.effect: Reweighting reduced the disparity in model performance across subgroups; overall accuracy effect not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: When we employed the bias mitigation strategy of reweighting, however, the disparity was reduced.

evidence.title: FairPlay: Improving Medical Machine Learning Models with Generative Balancing for Equity and Excellence
evidence.outcome: Subgroup fairness metrics and overall F1 after synthetic-data bias mitigation in mortality prediction
evidence.effect: F1 improved by up to 21% averaged across downstream models; improved for every subgroup; gap between subgroup performances shrank; both fairness metrics improved in all four setups.
evidence.quote: It achieves this across every subgroup while simultaneously shrinking the gap between different subgroup performances, as demonstrated through the universal improvement of a pair of fairness metrics across four different experimental setups.

evidence.title: Gender Bias When Using Artificial Intelligence to Assess Anorexia Nervosa on Social Media: Data-Driven Study
evidence.outcome: Effect of bias mitigation algorithms on gender disparities in FNR and accuracy
evidence.effect: Reweighting gave the best FNR ratio (4.636 to 2.591) but raised male FNR and reduced male accuracy; disparities mitigated but not eliminated; some methods no better than original.
evidence.quote: The results showed that, even when disparities can be mitigated with most of the algorithms, they cannot be eliminated.

evidence.title: Fair admission risk prediction with proportional multicalibration
evidence.outcome: calibration fairness and classification performance
evidence.effect: Controlled simultaneous calibration fairness over intersectional groups with virtually no cost in classification performance.
evidence.quote: We observe that proportional multicalibration is a promising criteria for controlling simultaneous measures of calibration fairness of a model over intersectional groups with virtually no cost in terms of classification performance.

evidence.title: Towards Fair Patient-Trial Matching via Patient-Criterion Level Fairness Constraint
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: Reduction of biased predictions in patient-trial matching with fairness constraint
evidence.effect: Reported qualitatively: the proposed fairness framework alleviated predictions tending to be biased on real-world patient-trial and patient-criterion matching tasks; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The experimental results on real-world patient-trial and patient-criterion matching tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework can successfully alleviate the predictions that tend to be biased.

evidence.title: Generative models improve fairness of medical classifiers under distribution shifts
evidence.outcome: Subgroup diagnostic accuracy and robustness with vs without synthetic augmentation, in and out of distribution
evidence.effect: Adding diffusion-generated synthetic samples improved robustness in all three tasks and improved accuracy within underrepresented groups, especially out of distribution. Numbers not given in the text.
evidence.quote: Complementing real samples with synthetic ones improved the robustness of models in all three medical tasks and increased fairness by improving the accuracy of clinical diagnosis within underrepresented groups, especially out of distribution.

evidence.title: Identify and mitigate bias in electronic phenotyping: A comprehensive study from computational perspective
evidence.outcome: Effect of bias mitigation strategies on fairness of pneumonia and sepsis phenotyping models
evidence.effect: Five mitigation strategies (pre-, in-, post-processing) were evaluated on 9 phenotyping methods; the abstract reports no quantitative results or direction of effect.
evidence.quote: In this work, we are motivated to bridge this gap through a comprehensive experimental study to identify the bias existing in electronic phenotyping models and evaluate the widely-used debiasing methods' performance on these models.

evidence.title: Towards objective and systematic evaluation of bias in artificial intelligence for medical imaging
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Subgroup TPR/FPR disparities and accuracy after bias mitigation strategies versus naive model
evidence.effect: Reweighing nearly eliminated disparities (near-bias relative ΔTPR 0.44%, ΔFPR -0.69%); unlearning reduced them less (ΔTPR 12.22%, ΔFPR 15.51%); overall accuracy comparable to naive; unlearning hurt the no-bias dataset.
evidence.quote: The reweighing strategy almost perfectly mitigated any measured performance disparity between the bias groups, to respective values of relative ΔTPR and relative ΔFPR of 0.44 ± 1.80% and −0.69 ± 1.45% for the Near Bias scenario, and −0.80 ± 0.64% and −0.32 ± 2.13% for the Far Bias scenario.

evidence.title: The limits of fair medical imaging AI in real-world generalization
evidence.outcome: Fairness gaps after algorithmic shortcut correction, in-distribution versus external test sets
evidence.effect: Algorithmic correction closed fairness gaps in the original data distribution ('locally optimal'), but this did not hold in new test settings; models with less demographic encoding were often more fair externally.
evidence.quote: Although correcting shortcuts algorithmically effectively addresses fairness gaps to create 'locally optimal' models within the original data distribution, this optimality is not true in new test settings.
evidence.sample_unit: datasets (six chest X-ray datasets plus dermatology and ophthalmology datasets)

evidence.title: Mitigating Sociodemographic Bias in Opioid Use Disorder Prediction: Fairness-Aware Machine Learning Framework
evidence.outcome: Reduction in subgroup performance bias after equality-of-odds mitigation, with overall accuracy and recall
evidence.effect: Bias fell by 21.66% (sex), 1.48% (race), 21.04% (income) with NN-SGD, and up to 41.62% (race) with NN-Adam. WMV classifier recall was 85.37% and 92.68%, accuracy 58.85% and 90.21%.
evidence.quote: Our bias mitigation algorithm substantially reduced bias with NN-SGD, by 21.66% for sex, 1.48% for race, and 21.04% for income, and with NN-Adam by 16.96% for sex, 8.87% for marital status, 8.45% for working condition, and 41.62% for race.
evidence.sample_unit: survey respondents (2020 National Survey on Drug Use and Health)

evidence.title: Evaluating machine learning model bias and racial disparities in non-small cell lung cancer using SEER registry data
evidence.outcome: Effect of stratified oversampling mitigation on disparate impact and model accuracy
evidence.effect: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.
evidence.quote: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.

evidence.title: Survival After Radical Cystectomy for Bladder Cancer: Development of a Fair Machine Learning Model
evidence.outcome: Equalized odds ratio and overall accuracy/F1 after applying bias mitigation techniques
evidence.effect: All 3 mitigation techniques raised eOR from 0.619 (correlation remover 0.750, threshold optimizer 0.750, exponentiated gradient 0.667) with F1 0.861 vs 0.860 for correlation remover; residual unfairness remained and some subgroups decreased.
evidence.quote: We found that all techniques improved the eOR, with the largest improvements observed after applying correlation remover and threshold optimizer; application of these techniques resulted in an equivalent eOR of 0.750 ( Table 4 ).

evidence.title: Mitigating Algorithmic Bias in AI-Driven Cardiovascular Imaging for Fairer Diagnostics
evidence.outcome: Fairness metrics and accuracy before vs after bias mitigation (adversarial debiasing, BPA, equalised odds)
evidence.effect: Disparate impact rose from 0.80 to 0.95 and equal opportunity difference fell from 0.20 to 0.05. BPA cut FPR for males 0.0059 to 0.0033 and females 0.0096 to 0.0064. Overall accuracy effect after mitigation not clearly reported.
evidence.quote: For example, disparate impact increased from 0.80 to 0.95, and equal opportunity difference decreased from 0.20 to 0.05, demonstrating significant reductions in demographic bias.

evidence.title: Accounting for racial bias and social determinants of health in a model of hypertension control
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Effect of race-specific decision thresholds on error-rate parity between Black and White patients
evidence.effect: Thresholds of 0.296 (Black) and 0.245 (White) equalized FNR at 25%; FPR became 41.11% vs 47.20%; FPR/FNR ratio factor 0.87 versus ~8 before. Weighted F1 fell to 65.77% and 60.91%.
evidence.quote: The resulting FPR of the model for Black patients becomes 41.11% and the FPR for White patient model becomes 47.20%.

evidence.title: FairDiffusion: Enhancing equity in latent diffusion models via fair Bayesian perturbation
evidence.outcome: Effect of the FairDiffusion bias mitigation on image quality and clinical feature alignment
evidence.effect: FairDiffusion improved both image quality and semantic alignment of clinical features; no numeric values are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: To reduce these biases, we propose FairDiffusion, an equity-aware latent diffusion model that improves both image quality and the semantic alignment of clinical features.

evidence.title: Generative AI mitigates representation bias and improves model fairness through synthetic health data
evidence.outcome: Downstream model fairness by subpopulation after synthetic-data bias mitigation
evidence.effect: Synthetic data from CA-GAN improved model fairness in Black patients and female patients, evaluated separately per subpopulation; predictive performance in the downstream task also improved.
evidence.quote: We show that synthetic data generated by our CA-GAN improves model fairness in Black patients as well as female patients when evaluated separately for each subpopulation.

evidence.title: FairICP: identifying biases and increasing transparency at the point of care in post-implementation clinical decision support using inductive conformal prediction
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and accuracy gap between privileged and unprivileged subgroups after FairICP mitigation versus baseline
evidence.effect: FairICP improved prediction accuracy by 7.2% and reduced the accuracy gap between privileged and unprivileged subpopulations by 2.2% on average across three datasets.
evidence.quote: Compared to the baseline, FairICP improved prediction accuracy by 7.2% and reduced the accuracy gap between the privileged and unprivileged subpopulations by 2.2% on average across all three datasets.

evidence.title: Enhancing Fairness in Large Language Models for Clinical Artificial Intelligence Applications Through Fine-Tuning and Prompting
evidence.outcome: Bias score across gender, race, profession, religion with debiased prompts and fine-tuning
evidence.effect: Debiased prompts reduce bias, and fine-tuning the model performs even better (lower bias scores).
evidence.quote: We also note that debiased prompts reduce bias, and fine-tuning the model performs even better.

evidence.title: Addressing the balance between fairness and performance in glioma grade prediction using bias mitigation techniques
evidence.outcome: Fairness metrics and prediction performance after reweighting and equalized-odds mitigation across race and gender groups
evidence.effect: For race, reweighting with logistic regression worsened outcomes for the under-represented group and increased unfairness, while equalized-odds post-processing improved results for the under-represented group and significantly improved fairness.
evidence.quote: For the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant improvements in fairness.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (TCGA glioma dataset; count not reported in text)

evidence.title: Bias Evaluation and Mitigation in Retrieval-Augmented Medical Question-Answering Systems
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: Effect of bias mitigation strategies on fairness metrics and accuracy
evidence.effect: Chain-of-Thought, Counterfactual filtering, Adversarial prompt refinement, and Majority Vote were compared; Majority Vote aggregation improved both accuracy and fairness metrics. No numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: Experimental results reveal significant demographic disparities, highlighting that Majority Vote aggregation improves accuracy and fairness metrics.

evidence.title: Integration of fairness-awareness into clinical language processing models
evidence.outcome: Effect of fairness-aware loss on subgroup parity and overall model performance across architectures
evidence.effect: Fairness constraints enhanced parity across most transformer architectures but degraded hierarchical model performance and caused one clinical model to collapse toward majority predictions.
evidence.quote: Fairness constraints enhance parity across most transformer architectures, but degrade hierarchical model performance and cause one clinical model to collapse toward majority predictions, demonstrating that fairness interventions are highly model dependent.

evidence.title: From Detection to Mitigation: Addressing Bias in Deep Learning Models for Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
evidence.venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
evidence.outcome: Subgroup fairness and overall predictive performance after bias mitigation (XGBoost retraining, active learning) across sex, age, race
evidence.effect: XGBoost final layer improved subgroup fairness while maintaining or improving overall performance; combining XGBoost retraining with active learning gave the largest bias reduction across all subgroups, in and out of distribution.
evidence.quote: We show that replacing the final layer of CNN with an eXtreme Gradient Boosting classifier improves the fairness of the subgroup while maintaining or improving the overall predictive performance.
evidence.sample_unit: chest X-ray images (CheXpert and MIMIC datasets)

evidence.title: Towards fair and trustworthy heart rate estimation from wrist-worn photoplethysmography: a multi-wavelength dataset and uncertainty-aware deep learning approach evaluated across skin tones, sexes, and motion conditions
evidence.outcome: MAE and skin-tone parity gap
evidence.effect: Uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and skin-tone parity gap from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM.
evidence.quote: Baseline error was higher for participants with darker skin tones and for females; uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated these gaps (reducing parity gaps from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM for skin tone).

evidence.title: Deep Learning Model Using Transfer Learning for Detecting Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction: Retrospective Algorithm Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Recalibration for subgroup degradation
evidence.effect: External follow-up 12-lead AUROC improved from 0.910 to 0.940; recalibration improvements were P<.001 across clinical subgroups.
evidence.quote: Recalibration yielded statistically significant improvements in the 12-lead DeepECG LVSD models (P<.001), with enhanced and more balanced performance across all clinical subgroups.

evidence.title: Evaluation Framework for Bruise Detection: Systematic ALS/White-Light Training and Skin-Tone Balancing with Deep Learning
evidence.outcome: Effect of skin-tone balancing on subgroup failure and overprediction rates
evidence.effect: Balancing significantly cut failure for Brown (12.3% to 2.9%, p=0.004), Dark (14.9% to 5.6%, p=0.019), Intermediate (p=0.012), but raised overprediction significantly in 5 of 6 tones by 8-15 percentage points.
evidence.quote: While skin-balanced training reduced failure rates in darker tones, it introduced a substantial and counterbalancing increase in overprediction rates ( Table 10 ).

evidence.title: Demographic-aware temporal graph attention for fair and accurate cardiac abnormality detection in 12-lead ECG
evidence.outcome: Effect of fairness regularization on subgroup disparity and overall accuracy
evidence.effect: Gap reduced from 15.42% to 1.75% while macro F1 0.8952 and AUROC 0.9762 surpassed all baselines.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on PTB-XL (21,507 recordings), DA-GAT-v2 achieves macro F1 of 0.8952 and AUROC of 0.9762, surpassing all compared baselines.

evidence.title: Attention guided fair artificial intelligence modeling for skin cancer diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Gender bias and diagnostic performance after applying bias mitigation versus existing mitigation algorithms
evidence.effect: LesionAttn significantly mitigated gender bias while maintaining high diagnostic performance, outperforming existing bias-mitigation algorithms on two datasets (numbers not reported in abstract).
evidence.quote: Validated on two large-scale dermatologic datasets for binary malignancy classification, LesionAttn significantly mitigated gender bias while maintaining high diagnostic performance, outperforming existing bias-mitigation algorithms.
evidence.sample_unit: dermatologic images (two large-scale datasets; count not reported)

evidence.title: Cross-Sensor and Cross-Population Generalization of Deep Learning Models for Digital Mammography: A Controlled Four-Country Benchmark of Five Backbone Architectures with Statistical Significance Testing
evidence.outcome: Effect of density-aware loss mitigation on AUC and calibration
evidence.effect: Density-aware focal loss reduced AUC by 0.031-0.061 and doubled ECE (0.055 to 0.104-0.116) at every weight.
evidence.quote: Adding the density-aware auxiliary loss degraded performance on every weight setting tested.
evidence.sample_unit: validation images (CBIS-DDSM; external: CMMD 1032, DMID 509, MIAS 322)

evidence.title: Mitigating medical bias in large language models by prompt engineering: an empirical study of effectiveness and trade-offs
evidence.venue: Philosophical transactions. Series A, Mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences
evidence.outcome: Change in accuracy gap between privileged and unprivileged groups under five prompting strategies across five LLMs
evidence.effect: Effectiveness heterogeneous across models with no strategy universally effective and some exacerbating bias. Chain-of-thought lowered the average gap by 2.4 percentage points (max 6.2 pp, DeepSeek-V3.1-sex); significant reductions in 8/15 cases by McNemar test.
evidence.quote: Results reveal substantial heterogeneity in both effectiveness and overhead across models, with no strategy proving universally effective and some even exacerbating bias.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark questions (medical bias benchmark; 5 prompting strategies x 5 LLMs x 15 scenarios)

evidence.title: Trustworthy AI for radar vital signs: detecting and mitigating gender bias in healthcare
evidence.outcome: Bias scores and F1/accuracy after TimeGAN augmentation, equalised-odds regularisation and threshold adjustment
evidence.effect: Bias reduced to as low as 0.00005 (from 0.0261 in abstract), p<0.001; post-mitigation accuracy 98.5-99.03%, F1 0.975-0.993. TimeGAN raised male-only F1 0.79 to 0.88.
evidence.quote: Performance remained high across configurations, indicating that bias reduction was achieved without substantial degradation in Accuracy, Precision, Recall, or F1-score.

evidence.title: From Biomedical Datasets to Fairness-Aware Recommendations: An Integrated Data Orchestration Pipeline for Binary Clinical Predictions
evidence.outcome: Subgroup gap reduction after mitigation with verification of balanced accuracy change
evidence.effect: ACTG175 gender combined gap improved by 0.190 (~55.8% relative reduction), BA +0.046; stroke aggregate gap reduction 39.41%, mean BA change −0.002, bootstrap P=0.00399.
evidence.quote: Aggregate combined FPR + FNR gap reduction of 39.41%; mean BA change −0.002; aggregate bootstrap P = 0.00399, so the aggregate reduction was statistically supported.

evidence.title: FairEnc: A Fair vision-language model with fair vision and text encoders for glaucoma detection
evidence.outcome: Demographic disparities (DPD, DEOdds) and diagnostic performance after fairness-aware pretraining for glaucoma detection
evidence.effect: FairEnc reduced demographic disparities measured by DPD and DEOdds while keeping strong diagnostic performance in zero-shot and linear probing; on FairFundus, performance stayed within a competitive range.
evidence.quote: Comprehensive experiments on the publicly available Harvard-FairVLMed dataset show that FairEnc reduces demographic disparities measured by DPD and DEOdds while achieving strong diagnostic performance under both zero-shot and linear probing evaluations.

evidence.title: Single-Axis Fairness Interventions Produce Asymmetric Cross-Axis Effects in Clinical Prediction
evidence.outcome: Bias mitigation effects on performance and calibration
evidence.effect: Race-targeting incurred greater performance costs and calibration loss; fairness gains potentially reflected leveling down.
evidence.quote: Race-targeting also incurred greater performance costs and calibration loss, with observed fairness gains potentially reflecting leveling down rather than genuine improvement.

evidence.title: Evaluating machine learning model bias and racial disparities in non-small cell lung cancer using SEER registry data
evidence.outcome: effect of stratified oversampling on disparate impact and accuracy
evidence.effect: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.
evidence.quote: Stratified oversampling strategies reduced disparate impact while reducing the accuracy of the model.

commentary.bottom_line: Of 74 studies testing bias mitigation, most report reduced subgroup disparities with small or no loss of accuracy, but nearly all are offline analyses and several show mitigation shifting bias to other groups or lowering performance for everyone. The evidence supports the recommendation's requirement to check fairness and accuracy together after any mitigation, across more than one subgroup axis.

perspectives.view: Only one study measured mitigation in a real deployment, where recalibration reduced miscalibration across subgroups in 49,282 patients. The remaining shown studies are offline or simulated. Results are inconsistent across methods and settings, and outcomes are model metrics rather than patient outcomes. Indirectness and inconsistency lead to low certainty.

In a simulation, error-rate parity methods cut the mortality rate ratio from 3.77 to about 3.05 by raising mortality in the privileged group. In one obstetric study, reweighing lowered sensitivity by about 0.25. Two benchmark studies also found fairness gains that came with accuracy or calibration loss. These results suggest that checking accuracy after mitigation may catch leveling down before deployment.

Prompt-based mitigation for language models gave variable results. One study found bias gaps falling from 45 to 27 points while accuracy rose, but one model got worse. In another, a ZIP-code income gap fell from 11.4 to 5.8 points and was not eliminated. These findings suggest each model and prompt needs re-testing after changes.

When reweighing targeted area deprivation, it introduced language bias. The equal opportunity ratio moved from 0.91 to 1.35 and predictive equality from 0.84 to 0.29, and race bias also worsened. This suggests mitigation on one axis can harm limited English proficiency patients unless all relevant subgroups are re-audited.

commentary.research_gap: No study shown links bias mitigation to patient outcomes in a live clinical deployment, and only one measured mitigation effects in real use. Prospective studies are needed that track fairness, accuracy, and harm across several subgroup axes at once after mitigation, including in safety-net settings.
commentary.underserved_note: Several offline tests included underserved groups. Two involved Medicaid populations, one included limited English proficiency and low health literacy patients, and a few involved low-income populations. The LEP study found that mitigation aimed at one group worsened bias against non-English speakers. No test was set in a safety-net system, so effects in those settings remain unmeasured.
